tools.name: beamwell
tools.description: A private 'send this to my phone' clipboard bridge: pair two of your own devices once (scan a QR or open a link), then beam text, links, one-time codes and images between them instantly — sent directly browser-to-browser and end-to-end encrypted, with nothing kept on any server. Peer discovery + signalling ride public nostr relays via trystero, with the handshake encrypted by the room passphrase so a relay sees only ciphertext; a four-word Short Authentication String catches a MITM relay. Each item is packed into a versioned envelope, sealed in AES-GCM-256 with a key derived from the passphrase, and framed as [iv|ciphertext] over a direct DTLS data channel. Text is auto-classified into link / one-time-code / plain text; images ride the same channel as a binary payload. Pairings are remembered locally (room + passphrase in localStorage) for one-tap reconnect and are forgettable any time. The camera QR scan (BarcodeDetector) is a sensor input, with open/paste-the-link as the first-class fallback; delivery receipts, tap-to-copy and save/Web-Share round it out.
browser_apis: WebRTC (RTCPeerConnection + data channels, via trystero) — a direct two-peer link; item frames travel browser-to-browser DTLS-encrypted with no server in the path; trystero auto-chunks the binary frames and reports send/receive progress

trystero (nostr strategy) — zero-backend peer discovery + signalling over public nostr relays; the room passphrase encrypts the whole handshake (SDP/ICE) so a relay can't read the offer/answer or swap DTLS fingerprints

Web Crypto (PBKDF2-SHA-256 → 32-byte room secret → AES-GCM-256 item key; every item's envelope sealed with a fresh 12-byte IV before it leaves and opened only on the far side; SHA-256 → a deterministic, symmetric four-word Short Authentication String — unit-tested for determinism + symmetry)

BarcodeDetector + getUserMedia (rear camera — the sensor input; reads the pairing QR on-device via a setInterval decode loop, permission requested inside a tap, every track stopped the moment a code is read / on teardown; open-or-paste-the-link is the first-class fallback when BarcodeDetector is absent or the camera is denied)

First-party versioned item envelope (unit-tested pure core): [version|headerLen|headerJSON|payload] carrying id/kind/at/text/name/mime + optional image bytes, and an [iv|ciphertext] frame packer/unpacker — the whole wire format is pure and unit-tested end-to-end
First-party item classifier (unit-tested): URL vs one-time-code vs plain-text detection so a beamed snippet is labelled and given the right copy affordance
First-party remembered-pairing store (unit-tested over injected storage): room+passphrase+name kept in localStorage for one-tap reconnect, upsert-by-room / touch / forget, corrupt-storage tolerant
qrcode (pairing QR) + Web Share API (level 2, link + received images) + Clipboard API (Beam-clipboard in; tap-to-copy received text/link/code out)
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker for a received image, anchor-download fallback)
localStorage (remembered pairings + device-name/remember preferences only; never item contents)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; installable, offline app shell)

tools.name: syncwell
tools.description: Private, end-to-end encrypted live folder sync between your own devices (laptop ↔ phone) or with one peer — no cloud, no account, nothing hosted. Pick a folder on each device with the File System Access API; edits propagate live over a direct WebRTC data channel (DTLS on the wire), and every file is additionally sealed in AES-GCM-256 with a key derived from the room passphrase, so the plaintext exists only inside the two tabs. Peer discovery + signalling ride public nostr relays via trystero, with the handshake encrypted by the passphrase so a relay sees only ciphertext; a four-word Short Authentication String catches a MITM relay. The protocol is pull-based (each side asks for what the other holds newer/unique, so no file is sent twice), diffs are computed from an encrypted manifest, and a version ledger prevents the write-mtime sync ping-pong. Syncwell never deletes — a peer can only add or update files. Direction control (two-way / send-only / receive-only); a files-only send/download path is the first-class fallback on non-Chromium browsers.
browser_apis: File System Access API (showDirectoryPicker readwrite — the input; recursive scan → manifest, per-file read, getDirectoryHandle({create})+createWritable to mirror incoming files to disk; drag-a-folder via DataTransferItem.getAsFileSystemHandle + requestPermission; polled every ~3s since there is no file-watch API)

WebRTC (RTCPeerConnection + data channels, via trystero) — a direct two-peer link; file frames travel browser-to-browser DTLS-encrypted with no server in the file path; trystero auto-chunks the binary frames and reports send/receive progress

trystero (nostr strategy) — zero-backend peer discovery + signalling over public nostr relays; the room passphrase encrypts the whole handshake (SDP/ICE) so a relay can't read the offer/answer or swap DTLS fingerprints

Web Crypto (PBKDF2-SHA-256 → 32-byte room secret → imported as an AES-GCM-256 key; every file's bytes sealed with a fresh 12-byte IV before they leave and opened only on the far side; SHA-256 per-file integrity check after decrypt; SHA-256 → a deterministic, symmetric four-word Short Authentication String — unit-tested)
Web Workers (dedicated crypto worker holding the AES key; all encrypt/decrypt/hash off the main thread; Transferable ArrayBuffers zero-copy the file bytes and frames in and out)

First-party pull-based sync engine (unit-tested pure cores): manifest diff (computeWanted / fulfillable — remote-newer/unique wins, same-mtime-different-size flagged as a conflict and left untouched), path-safety validator (rejects ../, absolute paths, drive letters, control chars, Windows reserved names — a hard write-boundary against a malicious peer), self-framing file envelope ([len][JSON header][ciphertext]), and a version ledger that reports a synced file's origin mtime so the File-System-Access write-mtime doesn't cause a sync ping-pong
First-party safety guarantee: Syncwell never deletes — a path vanishing from a peer's manifest is simply no longer offered; existing files are never removed
qrcode (pairing QR) + Web Share API (level 2) + Clipboard API (copy the pairing link, which carries room + passphrase only in the URL hash, never sent to a server)
Files-only fallback (non-Chromium): <input webkitdirectory> to read files to send + anchor-download to receive — a first-class path when showDirectoryPicker is unavailable
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; installable, offline app shell)

tools.name: castwell
tools.description: Private, end-to-end encrypted screen sharing from a link — broadcast your screen to viewers with no account, no download and nothing hosted. Full-mesh WebRTC means the screen pixels travel directly between browsers (DTLS-SRTP) with no media server in the path; peer discovery + signalling ride public nostr relays via trystero, with the handshake encrypted by the room passphrase so the relay sees only ciphertext. A four-word Short Authentication String (derived from the passphrase, matching on both sides) catches a MITM relay. Anyone in the room can present; viewers pick which presenter to watch via a thumbnail strip. Optional microphone narration is mixed into the share on-device. Any viewer can keep a local WebM clip or a PNG snapshot — the takeaway artefact, encoded on-device and never uploaded; a denied screen-capture falls back to a first-class view-only join.
browser_apis: Screen Capture API (getDisplayMedia — the input; the presenter picks a screen/window/tab in the browser's own picker, plus system/tab audio where the OS allows; captured inside the Share tap; every track stopped on stop-share/leave/pagehide)

WebRTC (RTCPeerConnection + data channels, full-mesh) — a broadcast: the presenter adds their screen stream and every viewer receives it directly, DTLS-SRTP encrypted, with no media server in the path

trystero (nostr strategy) — zero-backend peer discovery + signalling over public nostr relays; the room passphrase encrypts the whole handshake (SDP/ICE), so a relay cannot read the offer/answer or swap DTLS fingerprints

Web Crypto (PBKDF2-SHA-256 → 32-byte room secret; SHA-256 → a four-word Short Authentication String + room fingerprint; unit-tested for determinism + symmetry so both peers derive identical words, and a mismatched passphrase yields different words)

getUserMedia (optional microphone narration; requested inside a tap; mixed into the share and togglable mid-share by connecting/disconnecting its source node — no WebRTC renegotiation; every track stopped on teardown)

Web Audio MediaStreamDestination — sum captured system/tab audio and the mic into a single outgoing audio track on-device (always present, even when silent, so mic toggling needs no renegotiation) + AnalyserNode narration level meter (never connected to destination, so no feedback)

MediaRecorder — record the focused stream (a viewer's incoming screen, or the presenter's own share) directly to a local WebM at full resolution, no canvas re-encode; a cloned stream so swapping windows doesn't kill an in-flight clip; the artefact, never uploaded
Canvas 2D (drawImage → toBlob) — PNG snapshot of the live screen, the second on-device artefact
Screen Wake Lock API (keeps a presenting/watching device awake; re-acquired on visibilitychange)
Web Share API (level 2, files — share the invite link + recordings) + Clipboard API (copy the invite) + qrcode (invite QR)

First-party (unit-tested): room-id/passphrase generation, invite-link build/parse (room + pass live only in the URL hash, never sent to a server), thumbnail-strip column layout, narration-level shaping, recorder MIME/duration/byte helpers
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; installable, offline app shell)

tools.name: sentrywell
tools.description: Turn any browser into a private, motion-detecting security camera — it snaps a photo and records a clip only when something moves — or scan an existing video to find every stretch of movement, each with a timecode and thumbnail. Grid-based frame differencing runs entirely on-device; clips live in IndexedDB on this machine only and footage is never uploaded. Live mode adds a motion meter, sensitivity, a draggable detection zone, an optional local beep + system notification, and a screen wake lock; the file-scan path is the first-class fallback when the camera is denied.
browser_apis: getUserMedia (live camera + optional mic — the sensor input; echo-cancellation/noise-suppression/AGC off; every track stopped on disarm/pagehide; denied permission falls back to the first-class video-scan path)
First-party motion DSP (unit-tested): reduce each frame to a 20×15 luma grid, per-cell brightness differencing within an optional zone mask, sensitivity→(cellDelta, triggerFraction) mapping
First-party motion gate (unit-tested state machine): consecutive-frame debounce → start, cooldown/maxClip → stop; plus a segmentsFromScores grouper for the file path (peak-frame tracking)
MediaRecorder (+ isTypeSupported codec pick — vp9/vp8/webm, mp4 on Safari): motion-triggered clips encoded on-device, a fresh recorder per event so each clip is self-contained
Canvas 2D / OffscreenCanvas (downscaled 160×120 detection frame; full-res JPEG snapshots; overlay canvas for the detection-zone rectangle + live active-cell heat; 2× contact-sheet PNG)

HTMLVideoElement seek-stepping (file scan): frame-step an uploaded video by seeking, wait one presented frame via requestVideoFrameCallback — always raced against a timeout so a hidden tab can't hang the scan
Screen Wake Lock API (keeps a monitoring device awake while armed; re-acquired on visibilitychange)
Notifications API + Web Audio OscillatorNode (optional local 'motion detected' notification + two-tone beep; both device-local)
IndexedDB (captured events — snapshot + clip blobs — stored on this device only, with an in-memory fallback; one-click clear-all)
setInterval detection loop (a hidden tab throttles rAF to a halt; a background monitor must keep running)
Pointer Events (drag a normalized detection-zone rectangle over the video)
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker for clips/snapshots/CSV/JSON/PNG, anchor-download fallback)
Web Share API (level 2, files) + Clipboard API
First-party timeline CSV + segments JSON + contact-sheet PNG (the file-scan artefacts)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; app shell + sample clip precached, full offline)

tools.name: hushwell
tools.description: Remove background noise and hiss from voice recordings in your browser — the private answer to the cloud audio enhancers. On-device RNNoise (WebAssembly) streams the clip frame-by-frame, keeping the voice and suppressing steady hum/hiss/fans/traffic; a VAD-gated noise-floor estimate gives a real 'background reduced by N dB' number, a dry/wet strength slider re-mixes live, and you export a clean WAV or MP3. Input by file (audio, or a video's audio track) or by mic recording. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

AudioWorklet (import-free capture processor — raw mono Float32 PCM from the mic; never connected to the destination, so no monitoring feedback and nothing routes to the iOS earpiece; loaded as a same-origin asset to stay within CSP)

getUserMedia (mic recording requested inside a tap, echo-cancellation/noise-suppression/AGC off; every track stopped + context closed on stop/teardown/pagehide; denied permission falls back to file upload as a first-class path)
Web Workers (dedicated denoise loop streaming RNNoise frames off the main thread with determinate progress; separate WAV/MP3 encode worker)
Transferable ArrayBuffer (zero-copy PCM to/from the workers)
First-party DSP (unit-tested): downmix, linear resample, RMS/dBFS, VAD-gated low-percentile noise-floor estimate, dry/wet mix, peak-normalise
First-party 16-bit PCM WAV encoder + minimal WAV reader (the downloadable artefact + test round-trip)

tools.name: redactwell
tools.description: Black out text in a PDF permanently, in your browser — the covered words are physically removed, not just hidden. Drag black boxes or use Find & redact to place a box over every match of a word; redacted pages are rasterised and flattened to images so the text layer under each bar is destroyed, untouched pages are copied verbatim, and document metadata is dropped. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: pdf.js (pdfjs-dist) + its Web Worker — parse + render each page to a canvas, and extract the text layer (getTextContent + Util.transform) for Find & redact
Canvas 2D — rasterise each redacted page at the chosen DPI and paint the black bars into the pixels (padded to over-cover), so redaction is burned in rather than layered on top
pdf-lib in a dedicated Web Worker — rebuild the output PDF: embed flattened page images, copyPages untouched pages verbatim, and strip document metadata (author/title/producer)
First-party redaction geometry — normalized 0..1 boxes (orientation-agnostic), drag→box, pad/over-cover, page→pixel mapping, flatten-plan, DPI→scale (all unit-tested)
Pointer Events — draw / move / delete redaction rectangles, with a draw-vs-scroll mode toggle (touch-action none only in draw mode) so drawing and scrolling don't fight on a phone
IntersectionObserver — lazily render page canvases as they scroll into view
Transferable ArrayBuffer — zero-copy of the source bytes + rasterised page images to the assembly worker
requestAnimationFrame shim (native when visible, setTimeout when document.hidden) so an export keeps rendering when the tab is backgrounded — pdf.js schedules render continuations on rAF
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker for the PDF, anchor-download fallback)
Web Share API (level 2, files) + Clipboard-free download path
localStorage (export DPI / sharpness / flatten-all only; never the document)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; app shell + pdf.js worker + sample precached, full offline)

tools.name: embiggen
tools.description: Upscale and enhance small or low-resolution images in your browser with a Swin2SR super-resolution model — 2× or 4×, on WebGPU with a WASM fallback. Nothing is uploaded; the image never leaves the tab, and it works offline after the model downloads once.
browser_apis: @huggingface/transformers (Swin2SR image-to-image super-resolution; classical-x2 + realworld-x4 models, lazy-loaded per scale)
WebGPU (GPU inference) with automatic WASM/ONNX Runtime fallback
WebAssembly (ONNX Runtime Web, bundled same-origin — no CDN)
Web Workers + comlink (model + inference off the main thread)
First-party output-bound planning (pre-scale oversized inputs to keep the result ≤ 4096 px; Swin2SR has no tiling)
OffscreenCanvas + ImageData (decode via RawImage.fromBlob, encode PNG)
Pointer Events + clip-path (before/after compare slider, pointer + keyboard)
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker, with anchor-download fallback)
Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa; app shell precached, ORT wasm served not precached)

tools.name: swatchwell
tools.description: Pick colours from your camera or any image, build a palette, and export it as CSS, JSON, PNG, SVG, ASE or GPL. Real-world eyedropping via the rear camera, median-cut extraction from images, and the screen EyeDropper — with perceptual (CIEDE2000) nearest-name matching. Nothing is uploaded.
browser_apis: getUserMedia (rear camera — the live sensor input; torch constraint; tracks stopped on teardown/hide/unload)
EyeDropper API (screen-pixel sampling on desktop, feature-detected)
Canvas 2D / OffscreenCanvas + getImageData (reticle region sampling + PNG swatch-sheet render)
Web Workers + Transferable ArrayBuffer (first-party median-cut extraction, zero-copy)
First-party colour science (sRGB→linear→XYZ→Lab, CIEDE2000, HSL) — no runtime colour library
First-party Adobe Swatch Exchange (.ase) binary writer via DataView
File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker, with anchor-download fallback)

tools.name: shakewell
tools.description: Measure vibration frequency with your phone — turn the accelerometer into a live seismograph, spectrum analyser and RPM meter. Diagnose a wobbly washing machine, fan or motor; leave with a frequency, a spectrum PNG and a CSV. Nothing is uploaded.
browser_apis: DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission() (iOS 13+, requested inside a tap, feature-detected)
First-party radix-2 Cooley–Tukey FFT + Hann window + linear resampler (no runtime library)
Per-axis detrend + summed power spectra (avoids the |a| frequency-doubling artefact)
Parabolic sub-bin peak interpolation + integer-harmonic detection
Web Workers (large-CSV parse + full-recording FFT off the main thread)
Canvas 2D (live seismograph, live spectrum, off-screen 1200×675 PNG card)
setInterval render loop (a hidden tab throttles rAF to a halt)
File API + Blob + URL.createObjectURL (CSV in, CSV + PNG out)

tools.name: voxwell
tools.description: Change your voice in your browser — pitch and formants moved independently by a hand-written phase vocoder, live from the microphone or from a file, exported as WAV or MP3. Nothing is uploaded.
browser_apis: AudioWorklet (first-party phase vocoder: 1024-pt Hann STFT at 4× overlap, per-bin true-frequency estimation, spectral-envelope formant warp — no library)
AudioWorklet (second processor capturing raw Float32 PCM)
First-party radix-2 FFT (the worklet must be a single import-free ES module)
getUserMedia (mono, echoCancellation/noiseSuppression/AGC off; permission requested inside a tap)
OfflineAudioContext (file rendered through the identical graph, latency-trimmed)
GainNode with audio-rate gain (true ring modulation, not tremolo)
AnalyserNode + Canvas 2D (scope + level meter, setInterval-driven so a hidden tab can't stall it)

tools.name: meshprep
tools.description: Check a 3D model before you print it — size, volume, holes and non-manifold edges drawn in red on the model itself. Converts STL/OBJ/PLY/3MF. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: WebGL2 (first-party renderer, no three.js — flat shading from fragment-shader derivatives, no normal buffer; two-sided lighting so inverted-normal meshes stay visible)
Web Workers (parse → analyse → export off the main thread)
First-party format parsers (STL binary/ASCII, OBJ, PLY ASCII/binary both endiannesses, 3MF — a worker has no DOMParser)

tools.name: reactwell
tools.description: Drop a JSX or TSX file and see the React component render instantly — transpiled in your browser with esbuild (WASM) and mounted in a sandboxed iframe. React is bundled locally; nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: esbuild-wasm (in-browser JSX/TSX transpile + bundle, worker:false inside our worker)
Import maps + data: URL ES modules (resolve bare specifiers inside the sandbox)
Sandboxed <iframe srcdoc> (allow-scripts only, opaque origin; error boundary)
React 18 UMD (vendored same-origin, no CDN — preview runtime works offline)
postMessage (runtime/compile errors streamed from the frame)
File System Access API (showOpenFilePicker + poll-to-live-watch a file)
Clipboard API + Web Share API (share-by-URL snippet)
Service Worker (PWA; app shell precached, wasm runtime-cached)

tools.name: glyphcut
tools.description: Subset fonts and convert them to WOFF2 in your browser with HarfBuzz compiled to WebAssembly — keep only the characters your site uses. Licensed font files are never uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: WebAssembly (HarfBuzz hb-subset — harfbuzz-subset.wasm vendored same-origin, hand-written raw bindings)
Web Workers (whole font pipeline; fonts held worker-side for the session)
CSS Font Loading API (FontFace — live specimen rendered from the subsetted output)

tools.name: gridwell
tools.description: Open, query and convert huge CSV files in your browser — millions of rows filtered and exported with a real SQL engine (DuckDB) compiled to WebAssembly. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: @duckdb/duckdb-wasm (DuckDB analytical SQL engine, eh build — vendored same-origin, no CDN)
WebAssembly (exception-handling build; no cross-origin isolation required)
Web Workers (DuckDB's own worker — all queries off the main thread)
File API + registerFileHandle (BROWSER_FILEREADER ranged reads — file never buffered into JS memory)
Clipboard API (copy cell / SQL, paste-to-ingest CSV)
Service Worker (PWA; network-first shell, runtime-cached WASM)

tools.name: papershot
tools.description: Turn a phone photo of a document into a flat, readable PDF scan — corners found automatically, perspective flattened, shadows removed. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: First-party computer vision (Scharr gradient, convex hull, max-area quad, 4-point homography, bilinear inverse warp, integral-image adaptive threshold) — no OpenCV
Web Workers (whole CV pipeline; raw RGBA in and out)

tools.name: blurwell
tools.description: Blur faces in photos and video in your browser — automatic on-device face detection plus manual boxes for plates and badges, with the blur burned into the exported pixels. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
browser_apis: @mediapipe/tasks-vision (BlazeFace FaceDetector, WASM — model + runtime vendored same-origin)

tools.name: vidwell
tools.description: Compress and trim video in your browser — shrink a big MP4/MOV, cap the resolution, cut a clip, export a smaller MP4. Decode → H.264 encode happens on-device via WebCodecs; nothing is uploaded.

tools.name: verisum
tools.description: Compute and verify file checksums (SHA-256, SHA-512, MD5, BLAKE3…) in your browser — stream a file through a WASM hasher and match it against a published checksum. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: provenova
tools.description: The vendor-neutral system of record for quantum computing — capture, reproduce, benchmark, and attest quantum runs across any QPU or vendor.

tools.name: screenwell
tools.description: Record your screen — with mic, system audio and an optional webcam bubble — entirely in your browser. MediaRecorder encodes locally; nothing is uploaded. Works offline.

tools.name: pixpress
tools.description: Compress and convert images to WebP, JPEG, AVIF or PNG in your browser using @jsquash WASM encoders, with a before/after compare slider. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: inkwell
tools.description: Sign and fill PDFs entirely in your browser — draw/type/upload a signature, place text, dates, initials and checkmarks, download a flattened PDF. Nothing is uploaded.

tools.name: pagesmith
tools.description: Merge, split, reorder, rotate and delete PDF pages entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: unheic
tools.description: Convert iPhone HEIC & HEIF photos to JPG, PNG or WebP in your browser with libheif (WASM). No uploads; works offline.

tools.name: tokenpeek
tools.description: Decode, inspect, verify, crack weak HMAC secrets and forge JSON Web Tokens entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: scribewell
tools.description: Transcribe audio & video to text and subtitles (.srt/.vtt) entirely in your browser with OpenAI Whisper. No uploads, no accounts; works offline.

tools.name: gifsmith
tools.description: Turn any video into an animated GIF entirely in your browser. No uploads, no watermark; works offline.

tools.name: zipsafe
tools.description: Create and extract ZIP archives entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: veilpix
tools.description: Hide an AES-256 encrypted message or file inside an ordinary image via LSB steganography, in your browser. No uploads.

tools.name: sealbox
tools.description: Lock any file with a password in your browser using AES-256. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.

tools.name: metascrub
tools.description: Strip hidden metadata (GPS, camera serial, timestamps) from photos losslessly, in your browser. No uploads.

tools.name: bgwipe
tools.description: Erase image backgrounds in your browser with an in-browser ML model (RMBG-1.4). Photos never leave your device.

tools.name: pdf-crush
tools.description: Compress PDFs in your browser using MozJPEG WASM. No uploads, no accounts, no server.

tools.name: dropwell
tools.description: End-to-end encrypted peer-to-peer file sharing in the browser. No backend, no installs.

tools.name: qrforge
tools.description: Generate tracking-free QR codes and scan them, entirely in your browser. No uploads.

tools.name: textlift
tools.description: Extract text from images, screenshots and scanned PDFs entirely in your browser with Tesseract WASM — plain text or searchable PDF out. No uploads; English works offline.

tools.name: clipwell
tools.description: Trim audio into clips and ringtones in your browser — drag across the waveform, fade, normalise, export MP3 or WAV. Nothing is uploaded; works offline.
